cohort: 499 women in their first trimester of pregnancy
finding: Adequate levels of vitamin B12, 25OH-vitamin D, and folic acid in the first trimester of pregnancy were associated with a lower risk of caesarean delivery, meconium presence, and NICU admission.
mod_finding: Lower levels of vitamin B12, 25OH-vitamin D, and folic acid were associated with caesarean delivery, while higher ferritin levels were observed in the caesarean delivery group.
